name: Contrastive Learning (SimCLR, MoCo)
analogy: Think of it as a line-up game. The model is shown a chart and must pick out its own slightly altered twin from a line-up of thousands of other charts. To win, it has to learn what makes a chart itself and not any other, which is exactly the kind of description that later helps in grouping and forecasting.

steps.title: Make two altered views of each window
steps.description: Each window is copied twice, and each copy is changed a little in ways that should not change its meaning, such as noise, a small rescaling or some hidden bars. The two copies of one window are a positive pair.
steps.inExample: A 48-bar MNQ window gets a noisy copy and a masked copy; these two are the positive pair.

steps.title: Turn every view into a short vector
steps.description: A network reads each view and produces a vector of numbers, which is then scaled to unit length. Similarity between two views is the cosine of the angle between their vectors, so it only measures direction.
steps.inExample: Each view becomes a vector of 128 numbers; a batch of 1,024 windows gives 2,048 vectors.

steps.title: Gather the wrong answers
steps.description: Every view from a different window is a negative. The two methods differ in where negatives come from. SimCLR uses the other windows in a very large batch. MoCo keeps a stored pool of vectors from earlier steps, produced by a slow-moving copy of the network.
steps.inExample: In the SimCLR setting each noisy copy is compared against the 2,046 other views in its batch.

steps.title: Pull the pair together and push the rest away
steps.description: The model is rewarded when its view is far more similar to its own twin than to every negative. A temperature setting controls how sharply it must separate the twin from the crowd. Hard negatives, those that look similar, matter most.
steps.inExample: The twin's similarity rises from 35 percent to 90 percent over training while the best wrong match stays near 40 percent.

steps.title: Keep the stored pool fresh (MoCo)
steps.description: In MoCo, the stored pool is updated as training goes: new vectors enter and the oldest leave. The slow-moving copy produces these vectors so that they stay consistent with one another even though the main network keeps changing.
steps.inExample: A pool of 4,096 earlier window vectors is refreshed a batch at a time.

steps.title: Keep the backbone and drop the extras
steps.description: After training, only the part of the network before the final short layer is kept. Its output for a window serves as the learned description, ready for clustering, similarity search or a small labelled model.
steps.inExample: Today's window is described by the backbone's 256 numbers, then clustered with other windows.

useFor.example: Pretraining on years of MNQ and ES 5-minute windows before any direction labels are applied.
Clustering window descriptions into session types such as trend days, rotations and breakouts.
Fine-tuning a direction classifier from the backbone using a few months of labelled bars.
Ranking past windows by similarity to the current one to see what followed them.

avoidWhen: You cannot define alterations that keep a window's meaning; if the changes alter the market situation, the model learns to ignore real differences.
Your history is small; the method relies on many different windows to serve as informative wrong answers.

example.scenario: A researcher pretrains with the SimCLR style on two years of unlabelled MNQ 5-minute windows, batch size 1,024. At test time they check that a window's altered twin ranks first among the other views in its batch.

input.summary: A batch of windows, each with two altered views, plus a pool of other windows serving as wrong answers.

fields.name: windows per batch
fields.meaning: How many different windows are compared together; each one's twin is the right answer.

fields.name: window length
fields.meaning: Four hours of trading described to the model.

fields.name: features per bar
fields.meaning: Rescaled return, range, body share, wick balance, volume and related measures.

fields.name: views of each window
fields.meaning: A noisy copy and a masked copy of the same window.

fields.name: temperature setting
fields.meaning: How sharply the model must separate its twin from the other views.

output.summary: A description per window and a check on whether twins can be found in the crowd.

fields.name: window description
fields.meaning: The backbone output used by later models.

fields.name: similarity to the altered twin
fields.meaning: How alike the two views of the same window look to the model.

fields.name: rank of the twin among 2,047 candidate views
fields.meaning: The twin is the single most similar candidate, which is the goal of the game.

example.reading: Finding the twin first is evidence that the description captures what makes a window itself. It is not evidence of forecasting power. The proper test is a labelled model on top of the description compared with the same model on raw indicators over walk-forward folds, net of costs.
